children: Vystar’s revenue rose 198.5% year over year, while its net loss narrowed 66.3%. Revenue growth was driven by a bulk sale of Vytex products of approximately $54,000, and lower operating expenses—largely reduced share-based compensation to Blue Oar—contributed to the smaller loss.
¹ Reported as “Revenue”. ² Reported as “Net loss attributable to Vystar”. ³ Reported as “Basic and diluted loss per share: Net loss attributable to common shareholders”.
: Mattresses and toppers generated $54,607, or 89.8% of net revenue; air purification units contributed $6,233.
: Increased 313.9%, reflecting a $47,000 reduction in the Vytex inventory reserve and approximately $8,000 in insurance proceeds.
: Fell 48.1%, largely due to an approximately $90,000 decrease in share-based compensation to Blue Oar.
: Testing of the prototype integrating Fluid Energy conversion technology is expected to be completed by September 2027; production is expected in late 2027.
